in-calcutta-flag.title: The Calcutta Flag (1906)
desc:
- The Calcutta Flag (1906) was one of the earliest Indian nationalist flags, featuring three horizontal stripes of green, yellow, and red, with various emblems including the sun, crescent, and lotus
- Unfurled on 7 August 1906 at Parsee Bagan Square in Calcutta, it was designed to unify Hindus, Muslims, and Buddhists in the independence movement
- **Construction:** three horizontal bands — green (top, Islam), yellow (middle, Hinduism and Buddhism), and red (bottom)
- Eight lotus flowers on the top, sun and crescent on the middle band
- Ratio approximately 2:3
trivia:
- Early Indian independence flag used during the independence movement
- Represented the aspirations of Indian nationalists
- Evolved into the modern flag after independence

in-independence.title: Flag of the Indian Independence Movement
desc:
- The Indian independence movement flag (1931 version) featured saffron, white, and green horizontal stripes with a spinning wheel (charkha) centred — Mahatma Gandhi's symbol of self-reliance
- Adopted by the Indian National Congress in 1931, this flag evolved from earlier versions
- At independence in 1947, the charkha was replaced by the Ashoka Chakra to create the current national flag
- **Construction:** three equal horizontal bands of saffron (top), white, and green. A blue spinning wheel (charkha) centred on the white stripe. Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- India's independence flag (1947) represented freedom from British rule
- Designed by Pingali Venkayya
- The modern Indian flag is based on this independence flag

sikh-empire.title: Flag of the Sikh Empire
desc: - The Sikh Empire (1799–1849) used a triangular blue flag with a gold Khanda symbol, representing the martial and spiritual aspects of Sikh faith
- **Construction:** a triangular saffron or blue pennant bearing the Sikh Khanda emblem (double-edged sword, chakkar, and two kirpans)
trivia:
- The Sikh Empire (1799–1849) was founded by Maharaja Ranjit Singh
- Represented the height of Sikh military and political power
- Conquered significant territories in Punjab and beyond

british-raj.title: Flag of British India (Star of India)
desc: - The British Raj (1858–1947) used a blue ensign defaced with the Star of India emblem. It represented British rule over the Indian subcontinent
- **Construction:** a Blue Ensign or Red Ensign with the Star of India badge. Used as the flag of British India
trivia:
- The British Raj (1858–1947) was the period of direct British rule over India
- The Union Jack represented colonial authority over the Indian subcontinent
- Ended with Indian independence and the partition in 1947
